Five AI Tools.
One Unfinished Proposal.

Your team has AI. Why is the work still manual?

Setup: Summit Advisory Group, 150 employees. A $750,000 opportunity with Northstar Distribution for a 90-day operational improvement project. Five employees have completed correct Austin-only contributions. The client then adds Denver. Every figure, document and event is illustrative.

0:00–0:45 · Scene 1

Five completed contributions

Click Leah, Sam, Priya, Alex and Maya. Each card identifies the department, AI and business tool. Each has a realistic sample conversation, highlighted handoff and a document preview. Emphasize that all original outputs are correct for Austin.

“Everyone finished their AI work. So why isn’t the proposal finished?”

The five workspaces use three vendors: ChatGPT, Copilot and Claude. Do not imply five different AI vendors.

0:45–1:20 · Scene 2

The requirement changes after the work is complete

Read Rachel’s email: add Denver within 90 days, show the additional staffing and cost, keep the Friday proposal deadline. Leah acknowledges the complete request accurately. Click Record the client change.

“Nobody made a mistake. The client changed the requirement.”

1:20–2:30 · Scene 3

Show the work Leah still does

Click Walk the next manual handoff six times. Show collection, translation into requests, staffing/pricing reconciliation, legal review, assembly and approval chasing. This is the centerpiece. Leah is carrying the versions, assumptions and decisions between people who can each use AI successfully.

All six steps total 160 minutes of illustrative active coordination, plus waiting. “Up to three days” is an example, not a measured baseline. Do not claim a quantified saving for the connected version.

“AI finished five tasks. Leah is still doing the sixth: connecting them.”

2:30–4:30 · Scene 4

The connected workflow

  1. Click Trace the change. Show the common requirement revision and sample source imports.
  2. Select Leah and review the scope revision; approve as Leah.
  3. Select Sam. Review the extra 30 consultant-days and parallel staffing; approve as Sam.
  4. Select Priya. Review the proposed $810,000 fee, $495,000 delivery cost and 38.9% margin; approve as Priya.
  5. Select Alex. Review the revised locations, fee and scope; approve as Alex.
  6. Select Maya. Show the summary assembled from the approved inputs; approve as Maya.
  7. Select leadership and approve the complete packet.
  8. Click Apply approved updates. Show each simulated write being recorded and verified.

People approve judgment. The workflow connects the inputs, routes dependencies, tracks revisions and verifies completion. The named-owner buttons simulate decisions; they do not obtain real approval.

“We connected their work, their information, and their decisions.”

Optional Q&A exception tests
  • HubSpot update fails: choose the fault before applying updates. SharePoint saves, HubSpot fails, and release stays blocked. Select No fault and retry. The audit history shows SharePoint was not written twice.
  • New client revision: choose the revision fault before applying updates. A further location creates a new revision and invalidates prior approvals. Trace and review again. No stale proposal can be released.
  • Skip ahead: open scene 5 before completion. It remains blocked.
  • Open the build details to explain permitted connectors, shared requirements, a durable workflow, explicit release rules, human review, safe retries and measurement.
4:30–5:00 · Scene 5

A completed customer outcome

Show the consistent executive summary, six recorded decisions and three verified simulated updates. Read Leah’s unsent customer email. The download is a real local HTML summary generated from sample data, not a native Office export.

“We didn’t give these five employees another AI tool. They already had AI. We connected their work, their information, and their decisions. That’s the difference between AI making individual people more productive and AI making an entire company more productive.”

Close with the complimentary workflow assessment, scheduled separately after the webinar. Find manual handoffs, identify where AI can help, map the approvals and establish one real baseline metric.

What is real versus simulated

The UI, dependency gates, revision invalidation, partial-failure handling, audit history and HTML summary generation run locally. AI responses, source imports, commercial data, human approvals and writes to Microsoft 365, HubSpot and Kantata are simulated. No messages are sent. Live deployment would require configured authentication, permissions, connectors, evaluations and operational monitoring.
